{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "# https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/publishing-package-distribution-releases-using-github-actions-ci-cd-workflows/
name: Publish Python 🐍 distributions 📦 to PyPI and TestPyPI

on:
  - push

jobs:
  build-n-publish:
    name: Build and publish Python 🐍 distributions 📦 to PyPI and TestPyPI
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@master
      with:
        # https://github.com/actions/checkout#fetch-all-history-for-all-tags-and-branches
        fetch-depth: 0
    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v1
      with:
        python-version: "3.10"
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install pypa/build
      run: python -m pip install build --user
    - name: Build a binary wheel and a source tarball
      run: python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist/ .
    - name: Publish distribution 📦 to PyPI
      uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
      with:
        user: __token__
        password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
        print_hash: true
        verify_metadata: true", "rationale": "The workflow runs `python -m pip install build --user` on every tag push, repeatedly fetching the same dependency. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) is supported by measured evidence and fits this Python publishing job: it adds a pip cache keyed on the dependency manifest and runner OS, preserving all existing build/publish steps, permissions, secrets usage, and required checks without adding privileged actions, publishing changes, or new network access beyond the existing pip install.", "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]}
